messages.subject: Re: Masking by height from CHM
messages.body_plain:
Hi Eric,

Thanks for asking, using CHM to make mask is one point in my list of upgrades. I will try to do it as soon as possible and get back to you... ok

For now, you can make a simple mask by using a code like this:

mask<-CHM>5

In this case all pixels with height greater than 5m will be selected as TRUE (1) and others FALSE (0). On the next following steps, you will need to inform the parameter value=1. For example, on the fieldCount().

Let us know if it works... Hope it helps...!

All the best,
Filipe

messages.subject: Re: FIELDimageR: Re: Identificação dos Objetos
messages.body_plain:
Olá Felipe, bom dia!

Consegui realizar utilizando o seguinte comando:

a<-EX.Obj.D$x.position

df <- data.frame(matrix(unlist(a), nrow=length(a), byrow=TRUE))

DADO = df %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(Soma = (X1+X2),
         Soma1 = (X3+X4),
         CX = Soma/2,
         CY = Soma1/2)

text(DADO$CX, DADO$CY, rownames(DADO), col = "blue", cex = 0.8)

Abraço!

Raylson Mello

messages.subject: cropValue and cropAbove in fieldMask
messages.body_plain:
Hi Filipe, and Anyone who can help,

I would like to find out, in fieldMask(), does the function removes all values provided for cropValue when cropAbove is true? For instance, if cropValue = 0.5 and cropAbove = TRUE, would all values above 0.5 be considered as soil and hence removed?

Cheers,

Yussif.

messages.subject: Re: FIELDimageR: cropValue and cropAbove in fieldMask
messages.subject_clean: FIELDimageR: cropValue and cropAbove in fieldMask
messages.body_plain:
Good morning,  Yussif!

Yes, when  cropAbove  is =T (TRUE), it will delete all objects that are above this value.
When  cropAbove  is =F (FALSE), it will delete all objects that are below this value.

you make this assessment by the color of your objects of interest.

Cheers,
Raylson Melo
